Here \(n = \frac{1}{3}\) and \(x\) is replaced by \(-x\); the expansion holds for \(|x| < 1\).
\((1-x)^{1/3} = 1 + \frac{1}{3}(-x) + \frac{\frac{1}{3}\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right)}{2!}(-x)^{2} + \frac{\frac{1}{3}\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right)\left(-\frac{5}{3}\right)}{3!}(-x)^{3} + \cdots\)
\(= 1 - \frac{x}{3} + \left(-\frac{1}{9}\right)x^{2} + \frac{5}{81}\left(-x^{3}\right) + \cdots\)
\(\therefore (1-x)^{1/3} = 1 - \frac{x}{3} - \frac{x^{2}}{9} - \frac{5x^{3}}{81} - \cdots\)

Here \(n = -\frac{1}{5}\), and the expansion holds for \(|x| < 1\).
\((1+x)^{-1/5} = 1 + \left(-\frac{1}{5}\right)x + \frac{\left(-\frac{1}{5}\right)\left(-\frac{6}{5}\right)}{2!}x^{2} + \frac{\left(-\frac{1}{5}\right)\left(-\frac{6}{5}\right)\left(-\frac{11}{5}\right)}{3!}x^{3} + \cdots\)
\(= 1 - \frac{x}{5} + \frac{6/25}{2}x^{2} - \frac{66/125}{6}x^{3} + \cdots\)
\(\therefore (1+x)^{-1/5} = 1 - \frac{x}{5} + \frac{3x^{2}}{25} - \frac{11x^{3}}{125} + \cdots\)

Here \(n = -1\) and \(x\) is replaced by \(x^{2}\). The expansion holds for \(\left|x^{2}\right| < 1\), i.e. \(|x| < 1\).
\((1+x^{2})^{-1} = 1 + (-1)x^{2} + \frac{(-1)(-2)}{2!}(x^{2})^{2} + \frac{(-1)(-2)(-3)}{3!}(x^{2})^{3} + \cdots\)
\(= 1 - x^{2} + x^{4} - x^{6} + \cdots\)
(This is the geometric series with ratio \(-x^{2}\), as expected.)
\(\therefore (1+x^{2})^{-1} = 1 - x^{2} + x^{4} - x^{6} + \cdots\)

First bring it to the form \((1+t)^{n}\) by taking \(a\) out:
\((a-b)^{-3} = a^{-3}\left(1-\frac{b}{a}\right)^{-3}\), valid for \(\left|\frac{b}{a}\right| < 1\), i.e. \(|b| < |a|\).
With \(n = -3\) and \(x\) replaced by \(-\frac{b}{a}\),
\(\left(1-\frac{b}{a}\right)^{-3} = 1 + (-3)\left(-\frac{b}{a}\right) + \frac{(-3)(-4)}{2!}\left(-\frac{b}{a}\right)^{2} + \frac{(-3)(-4)(-5)}{3!}\left(-\frac{b}{a}\right)^{3} + \cdots\)
\(= 1 + \frac{3b}{a} + \frac{6b^{2}}{a^{2}} + \frac{10b^{3}}{a^{3}} + \cdots\)
\(\therefore (a-b)^{-3} = a^{-3}\left[1 + \frac{3b}{a} + \frac{6b^{2}}{a^{2}} + \frac{10b^{3}}{a^{3}} + \cdots\right]\)

Take \(a\) out: \((a+b)^{1/4} = a^{1/4}\left(1+\frac{b}{a}\right)^{1/4}\), valid for \(\left|\frac{b}{a}\right| < 1\), i.e. \(|b| < |a|\).
With \(n = \frac{1}{4}\) and \(x\) replaced by \(\frac{b}{a}\),
\(\left(1+\frac{b}{a}\right)^{1/4} = 1 + \frac{1}{4}\cdot\frac{b}{a} + \frac{\frac{1}{4}\left(-\frac{3}{4}\right)}{2!}\cdot\frac{b^{2}}{a^{2}} + \frac{\frac{1}{4}\left(-\frac{3}{4}\right)\left(-\frac{7}{4}\right)}{3!}\cdot\frac{b^{3}}{a^{3}} + \cdots\)
\(= 1 + \frac{b}{4a} - \frac{3b^{2}}{32a^{2}} + \frac{7b^{3}}{128a^{3}} + \cdots\)
\(\therefore (a+b)^{1/4} = a^{1/4}\left[1 + \frac{b}{4a} - \frac{3b^{2}}{32a^{2}} + \frac{7b^{3}}{128a^{3}} + \cdots\right]\)

Take \(a\) out: \((a-b)^{-1/4} = a^{-1/4}\left(1-\frac{b}{a}\right)^{-1/4}\), valid for \(\left|\frac{b}{a}\right| < 1\), i.e. \(|b| < |a|\).
With \(n = -\frac{1}{4}\) and \(x\) replaced by \(-\frac{b}{a}\),
\(\left(1-\frac{b}{a}\right)^{-1/4} = 1 + \left(-\frac{1}{4}\right)\left(-\frac{b}{a}\right) + \frac{\left(-\frac{1}{4}\right)\left(-\frac{5}{4}\right)}{2!}\left(-\frac{b}{a}\right)^{2} + \frac{\left(-\frac{1}{4}\right)\left(-\frac{5}{4}\right)\left(-\frac{9}{4}\right)}{3!}\left(-\frac{b}{a}\right)^{3} + \cdots\)
\(= 1 + \frac{b}{4a} + \frac{5b^{2}}{32a^{2}} + \left(-\frac{15}{128}\right)\left(-\frac{b^{3}}{a^{3}}\right) + \cdots\)
\(\therefore (a-b)^{-1/4} = a^{-1/4}\left[1 + \frac{b}{4a} + \frac{5b^{2}}{32a^{2}} + \frac{15b^{3}}{128a^{3}} + \cdots\right]\)

Take \(a\) out: \((a+b)^{-1/3} = a^{-1/3}\left(1+\frac{b}{a}\right)^{-1/3}\), valid for \(\left|\frac{b}{a}\right| < 1\), i.e. \(|b| < |a|\).
With \(n = -\frac{1}{3}\) and \(x\) replaced by \(\frac{b}{a}\),
\(\left(1+\frac{b}{a}\right)^{-1/3} = 1 + \left(-\frac{1}{3}\right)\frac{b}{a} + \frac{\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right)\left(-\frac{4}{3}\right)}{2!}\cdot\frac{b^{2}}{a^{2}} + \frac{\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right)\left(-\frac{4}{3}\right)\left(-\frac{7}{3}\right)}{3!}\cdot\frac{b^{3}}{a^{3}} + \cdots\)
\(= 1 - \frac{b}{3a} + \frac{2b^{2}}{9a^{2}} - \frac{14b^{3}}{81a^{3}} + \cdots\)
\(\therefore (a+b)^{-1/3} = a^{-1/3}\left[1 - \frac{b}{3a} + \frac{2b^{2}}{9a^{2}} - \frac{14b^{3}}{81a^{3}} + \cdots\right]\)

Here \(n = -\frac{1}{2}\) and \(x\) is replaced by \(3x\); the expansion holds for \(|3x| < 1\), i.e. \(|x| < \frac{1}{3}\).
\((1+3x)^{-1/2} = 1 + \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)(3x) + \frac{\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)}{2!}(3x)^{2} + \cdots\)
\(= 1 - \frac{3x}{2} + \frac{3}{8}\left(9x^{2}\right) + \cdots\)
\(\therefore (1+3x)^{-1/2} = 1 - \frac{3x}{2} + \frac{27x^{2}}{8} + \cdots\)

Take the constant \(2\) out first so the bracket becomes \((1+t)^{n}\):
\((2-3x)^{1/3} = 2^{1/3}\left(1-\frac{3x}{2}\right)^{1/3}\), valid for \(\left|\frac{3x}{2}\right| < 1\), i.e. \(|x| < \frac{2}{3}\).
With \(n = \frac{1}{3}\) and \(x\) replaced by \(-\frac{3x}{2}\),
\(\left(1-\frac{3x}{2}\right)^{1/3} = 1 + \frac{1}{3}\left(-\frac{3x}{2}\right) + \frac{\frac{1}{3}\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right)}{2!}\left(-\frac{3x}{2}\right)^{2} + \cdots = 1 - \frac{x}{2} - \frac{1}{9}\cdot\frac{9x^{2}}{4} + \cdots\)
\(\therefore (2-3x)^{1/3} = 2^{1/3}\left(1 - \frac{x}{2} - \frac{x^{2}}{4} + \cdots\right)\)

Take the constant \(5\) out first:
\((5+4x)^{-1/2} = 5^{-1/2}\left(1+\frac{4x}{5}\right)^{-1/2}\), valid for \(\left|\frac{4x}{5}\right| < 1\), i.e. \(|x| < \frac{5}{4}\).
With \(n = -\frac{1}{2}\) and \(x\) replaced by \(\frac{4x}{5}\),
\(\left(1+\frac{4x}{5}\right)^{-1/2} = 1 + \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)\frac{4x}{5} + \frac{\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)}{2!}\cdot\frac{16x^{2}}{25} + \cdots = 1 - \frac{2x}{5} + \frac{3}{8}\cdot\frac{16x^{2}}{25} + \cdots\)
\(\therefore (5+4x)^{-1/2} = 5^{-1/2}\left(1 - \frac{2x}{5} + \frac{6x^{2}}{25} + \cdots\right)\)

Take the constant \(5\) out first:
\((5-3x)^{-1/3} = 5^{-1/3}\left(1-\frac{3x}{5}\right)^{-1/3}\), valid for \(\left|\frac{3x}{5}\right| < 1\), i.e. \(|x| < \frac{5}{3}\).
With \(n = -\frac{1}{3}\) and \(x\) replaced by \(-\frac{3x}{5}\),
\(\left(1-\frac{3x}{5}\right)^{-1/3} = 1 + \left(-\frac{1}{3}\right)\left(-\frac{3x}{5}\right) + \frac{\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right)\left(-\frac{4}{3}\right)}{2!}\cdot\frac{9x^{2}}{25} + \cdots = 1 + \frac{x}{5} + \frac{2}{9}\cdot\frac{9x^{2}}{25} + \cdots\)
\(\therefore (5-3x)^{-1/3} = 5^{-1/3}\left(1 + \frac{x}{5} + \frac{2x^{2}}{25} + \cdots\right)\)

Split off the nearest perfect square so that the correction term is small:
\(\sqrt{99} = \sqrt{100-1} = \sqrt{100\left(1-\frac{1}{100}\right)} = 10(1-0.01)^{1/2}\), and \(|-0.01| < 1\).
With \(n = \frac{1}{2}\) and \(x\) replaced by \(-0.01\),
\((1-0.01)^{1/2} = 1 + \frac{1}{2}(-0.01) + \frac{\frac{1}{2}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)}{2!}(-0.01)^{2} + \frac{\frac{1}{2}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)}{3!}(-0.01)^{3} + \cdots\)
\(= 1 - 0.005 - 0.0000125 - 0.0000000625 - \cdots = 0.99498744\)
So \(\sqrt{99} = 10 \times 0.99498744 = 9.9498744\)
\(\therefore \sqrt{99} = 9.9499\) (correct to four decimal places).
